text:
Identify the correct order for the given property for following compounds.


[IMG]


Choose the correct answer from the option given below :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) Boiling point rises with the size of the alkyl group (larger surface, stronger van der Waals forces): $\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}<\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}<\mathrm{CH}{}_{3}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{Cl}$. Correct.

(B) For the same alkyl group, density rises with the atomic mass of the halogen: $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{Cl}<\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{Br}<\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{I}$. The given order places $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{Br}$ below $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{Cl}$. Incorrect.

(C) Each added Br atom raises the molar mass by about 80 u and strongly increases the van der Waals forces, so bromoethane  1-chloro-2-methylpropane > 2-chloro-2-methylpropane. Correct.

Statements (A), (C) and (E) are correct.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text: Number of cyclic tripeptides formed with 2 amino acids A and B is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In a cyclic tripeptide the three residues form a ring joined head to tail, so sequences that differ only by a rotation of the ring are the same molecule; for example $\text{A-A-B}$, $\text{A-B-A}$ and $\text{B-A-A}$ give one ring.

For three residues, each composition can be arranged in a ring in only one way, and reading the ring in the opposite direction gives one of its own rotations. The distinct rings are therefore one for each composition: $\text{cyclo(AAA)}$, $\text{cyclo(AAB)}$, $\text{cyclo(ABB)}$ and $\text{cyclo(BBB)}$, i.e. 4.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

$\frac{1}{λ_{\mathrm{He}+}}=\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}\times 2^{2}\times \left (\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{9}\right )...(2)$

$\begin{array}{l} λ_{\mathrm{He}^{+}}=λ\times \dfrac{9}{5} \\ λ_{\mathrm{He}^{+}}=\dfrac{9λ}{5} \end{array}$

text:
Chiral complex from the following is :

Here en = ethylene diamine
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $[\mathrm{PtCl}{}_{2}(\mathrm{en}){}_{2}]{}^{2+}$, Pt is in the +4 state and six-coordinate, so the complex is octahedral of the type $\mathrm{M}(\mathrm{AA})_{2}\mathrm{b}_{2}$.

In the cis isomer the two Cl are adjacent and the two en rings are arranged like a propeller; it has neither a mirror plane nor a centre of symmetry, so it is non-superimposable on its mirror image and is chiral.


[IMG]

trans-$[\mathrm{PtCl}{}_{2}(\mathrm{en}){}_{2}]{}^{2+}$ has a mirror plane containing Pt and both en rings, and trans-$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{4}\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}]{}^{+}$ has several mirror planes, so both are achiral; cis-$[\mathrm{PtCl}{}_{2}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{2}]$ is square planar Pt(II), and its molecular plane is a mirror plane.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

text: The standard electrode potential $(\mathrm{M}^{3+}/\mathrm{M}^{2+})$ for V, Cr, Mn & Co are $-$0.26 V, $-$0.41 V, + 1.57 V and + 1.97 V, respectively. The metal ions which can liberate $\mathrm{H}_{2}$ from a dilute acid are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
An ion $\mathrm{M}{}^{2+}$ liberates $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$ from dilute acid if it reduces $\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$, i.e. if $2~\mathrm{M}{}^{2+}+2\mathrm{H}{}^{+}\longrightarrow 2\mathrm{M}{}^{3+}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$ is spontaneous:

$E_{\text{cell}}^{\circ }=E_{\mathrm{H}{}^{+}/\mathrm{H}{}_{2}}^{\circ }-E_{\mathrm{M}{}^{3+}/\mathrm{M}{}^{2+}}^{\circ }=0-E_{\mathrm{M}{}^{3+}/\mathrm{M}{}^{2+}}^{\circ }$

This is positive only when $E_{\mathrm{M}{}^{3+}/\mathrm{M}{}^{2+}}^{\circ }$ is negative.

For V, $E_{\text{cell}}^{\circ }=+0.26\text{V}$ and for Cr, $+0.41\text{V}$, so $\mathrm{V}{}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Cr}{}^{2+}$ reduce $\mathrm{H}{}^{+}$ to $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$.

For Mn ($-1.57\text{V}$) and Co ($-1.97\text{V}$), $E_{\text{cell}}^{\circ }$ is negative: $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{2+}$ and $\mathrm{Co}{}^{2+}$ are stable, and $\mathrm{Mn}{}^{3+}$ and $\mathrm{Co}{}^{3+}$ are strong oxidising agents instead.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text:
For certain chemical reaction $X\to Y$, the rate of formation of product is plotted against the time as shown in the figure. The number of $\mathrm{correct}–$ statement/s from the following is $___________$.


[IMG]


(A) Over all order of this reaction is one.

(B) Order of this reaction can't be determined.

(C) In region I and III, the reaction is of first and zero order respectively.

(D) In region-II, the reaction is of first order.

(E) In region-II, the order of reaction is in the range of 0.1 to 0.9.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The rate of formation of Y is $r=k[\mathrm{X}]^{n}$, and $[\mathrm{X}]$ only decreases as time passes.

In regions I and II the rate increases with time while $[\mathrm{X}]$ falls, which is possible only for a negative order; a first-order reaction would show a rate falling exponentially with time. Hence (C), (D) and (E) are incorrect.

In region III the rate stays constant while $[\mathrm{X}]$ falls, so the reaction is zero order in that region.

The apparent order changes from region to region, so no single overall order can be assigned: (A) is incorrect and (B) is correct.

Only statement (B) is correct.

Hence, the answer is 1.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text:
Solid Lead nitrate is dissolved in 1 litre of water. The solution was found to boil at 100.15${}^{\circ }$C. When 0.2 mol of NaCl is added to the resulting solution, it was observed that the solution froze at $-0.8^{\circ }$ C. The solubility product of PbCl${}_{2}$ formed is $__________$ $\times$ 10${}^{-6}$ at 298 K. (Nearest integer)

Given : $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{b}}=0.5$ K kg mol${}^{-1}$ and $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{f}}=1.8$ K kg mol${}^{-1}$. Assume molality to be equal to molarity in all cases.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Lead nitrate gives three ions, $\mathrm{Pb}(\mathrm{NO}{}_{3}){}_{2}\longrightarrow \mathrm{Pb}{}^{2+}+2\mathrm{NO}{}_{3}{}^{-}$, so $i=3$ and

$0.15=3\times 0.5\times m\Rightarrow m=0.1\text{mol kg}^{-1}$

The $0.1$ mol of $\mathrm{Pb}(\mathrm{NO}{}_{3}){}_{2}$ reacts exactly with the $0.2$ mol of NaCl:

$\mathrm{Pb}(\mathrm{NO}{}_{3}){}_{2}+2\mathrm{NaCl}\longrightarrow \mathrm{PbCl}{}_{2}+2\mathrm{NaNO}{}_{3}$

This leaves $0.2$ mol of $\mathrm{NaNO}{}_{3}$, that is $0.4$ mol of ions, and $\mathrm{PbCl}{}_{2}$, of which $s$ mol L${}^{-1}$ stays dissolved as $\mathrm{Pb}{}^{2+}$ and $2~\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}$, that is $3s$ mol of ions.

$\Delta T_{f}=K_{f}m_{\text{ions}}\Rightarrow 0.8=1.8(0.4+3s)$

$0.4+3s=0.4444\Rightarrow s=0.0148\text{mol L}^{-1}$

$K_{sp}=[\mathrm{Pb}{}^{2+}][\mathrm{Cl}{}^{-}]^{2}=s(2s)^{2}=4s^{3}=4\times (0.0148)^{3}=1.30\times 10^{-5}\approx 13\times 10^{-6}$

Hence, the answer is 13.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text:
Water decomposes at 2300 K

$\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}(\mathrm{g})\to \mathrm{H}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}_{2}(\mathrm{g})$

The percent of water decomposing at 2300 K and 1 bar is $___________ ($Nearest integer).

Equilibrium constant for the reaction is $2\times 10^{-3}$ at 2300 K.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}⟶\mathrm{H}_{2}+\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{O}_{2}$

$\begin{array}{l} \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}=\dfrac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{T}}^{\frac{3}{2}}\left (1+\frac{α}{2}\right )α^{\frac{3}{2}}}{2^{\frac{1}{2}}\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{T}}\left (1+\frac{α}{2}\right )^{\frac{3}{2}}(1-α)} \\  \\ 2\times 10^{-3}=\dfrac{α^{\frac{3}{2}}}{2^{\frac{1}{2}}}[\text{as}α<<1\text{and let}\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{T}}=1] \end{array}$

$\begin{array}{l} α^{\frac{3}{2}}=2^{\frac{3}{2}}\times 10^{-3} \\  \\ \approx 2\times 10^{-2} \end{array}$

$\therefore %$ of water decomposition $=2%$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text:
Consider the following reaction approaching equilibrium at 27${}^{\circ }$C and 1 atm pressure

$\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}$ $⇌_{k_{r}=10^{2}}^{k_{f}=10^{3}}$ $\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{D}$

The standard Gibb's energy change $(\Delta _{\mathrm{r}}\mathrm{G}^{θ})$ at 27${}^{\circ }$C is ($-) ___________ kJ$ mol${}^{-1}$ (Nearest integer).

(Given : $\mathrm{R}=8.3\mathrm{J}\mathrm{K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ and $\ln 10=2.3$)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The Gibbs energy change for a reaction at standard conditions, $\Delta _{r}G^{θ}$, can be calculated using the equation:

$\Delta \mathrm{G}^{θ}=-\mathrm{RT}\ln \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{eq}}$

Where $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equilibrium constant given by $\frac{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{f}}}{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{b}}}$. For the reaction:

$\mathrm{A}+\mathrm{B}⇌\mathrm{C}+\mathrm{D}$

The forward rate constant, $k_{f}$, is $10^{3}$, and the reverse rate constant, $k_{r}$, is $10^{2}$. Therefore,

$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{eq}}=\frac{10^{3}}{10^{2}}=10$

Substitute the values into the Gibbs energy change formula:

$\Delta \mathrm{G}^{θ}=-\mathrm{RT}\ln 10$

where $R=8.3\mathrm{J}\mathrm{K}^{-1}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$ and $T=300\mathrm{K}$ (since the temperature is $27^{\circ }\mathrm{C}$ which converts to 300 K). The natural logarithm of 10 is approximately 2.3.

$\Delta \mathrm{G}^{θ}=-(8.3\times 300\times 2.3)$

Calculating gives:

$\Delta \mathrm{G}^{θ}=-5727\mathrm{J}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

Converting to kJ:

$\Delta \mathrm{G}^{θ}=-5.7\mathrm{kJ}\quad \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$

Rounding to the nearest integer, the standard Gibb's energy change is approximately $-6\mathrm{kJ}\quad \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift

text: The sum of bridging carbonyls in $\mathrm{W}(\mathrm{CO})_{6}$ and $\mathrm{Mn}_{2}(\mathrm{CO})_{10}$ is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{W}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{6}$ is a mononuclear octahedral carbonyl in which all six CO ligands are terminal, so it has no bridging CO.

$\mathrm{Mn}{}_{2}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{10}$ has the structure $(\mathrm{CO}){}_{5}\mathrm{Mn}-\mathrm{Mn}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{5}$: the two Mn atoms are held together only by a Mn–Mn bond, and all ten CO ligands are terminal, five on each Mn, so it also has no bridging CO.

Sum of bridging carbonyls $=0+0=0$.

Hence, the answer is 0.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2023 (Online) 29th January Morning Shift
